🌐 Q001: Chemical Weathering: Oceanic Geochemistry & Na-K Partitioning

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Arthur Holmes (Principles of Physical Geology, pp. 380–395); Krauskopf & Bird (Introduction to Geochemistry, Ch. 13); Faure (Principles of Geochemistry)
Official Examination Question — Question 1
Although sodium and potassium have approximately equal concentrations in nature, the waters of the seas and oceans are relatively strongly enriched in sodium because :
(A) the potash feldspars have low stability relative to plagioclase feldspar
(B) sodium is chemically more reactive than potassium
(C) potassium enters readily into newly formed clay minerals while sodium tends to remain in solution  ✔
(D) sodium is NOT particularly stable in the weathering environment and therefore passes into solution
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Chemical Weathering: Oceanic Geochemistry & Na-K Partitioning: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Chemical Weathering: Oceanic Geochemistry & Na-K Partitioning represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): potassium enters readily into newly formed clay minerals while sodium tends to remain in solution.

While crustal rocks supply equal stoichiometric amounts of Na and K during silicate weathering, potassium ions (K+) have a lower hydrated ionic radius and high charge density, causing them to be preferentially adsorbed into the interlayer sites of illite and smectite clays, while sodium (Na+) remains conservatively dissolved in oceanic water.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (C) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Arthur Holmes (Principles of Physical Geology, pp. 380–395); Krauskopf & Bird (Introduction to Geochemistry, Ch. 13); Faure (Principles of Geochemistry)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\text{Weathering Flux:} \quad 2\text{KAlSi}_3\text{O}_8 + 2\text{H}^+ + 9\text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow \text{Al}_2\text{Si}_2\text{O}_5(\text{OH})_4\ (\text{Kaolinite}) + 2\text{K}^+ + 4\text{H}_4\text{SiO}_4$$
PART II
Official Examination Question & Forensic Option Dissection
Rigorous analysis of each choice and justification of the verified answer
✔ VERIFIED ANSWER
Option (C) — potassium enters readily into newly formed clay minerals while sodium tends to remain in solution
Comprehensive Option-by-Option Forensic Breakdown
Option (A): the potash feldspars have low stability relative to plagioclase feldspar Incorrect Distractor
Why Option (A) is incorrect: While representing a prominent geological concept or landform in Earth science, Option (A) does not satisfy the specific hydrodynamic, climatic, or thermodynamic conditions posed in Question 1. Standard geomorphic literature confirms that Option (C) uniquely satisfies the diagnostic criteria.
Option (B): sodium is chemically more reactive than potassium Incorrect Distractor

Much of the aluminium is taken up by the clay minerals to form clay-rich rocks III. Formation of residual deposits leads to the concentration of aluminium in sedimentary rocks

(A) olivine weathers to pyroxene and pyroxene weathers to hornblende
(B) olivine, pyroxene and hornblende have equal susceptibility to weathering
(C) minerals rich in Si-O are least resistant to chemical weathering

(A) Ventifacts
(B) Brazil nuts
(C) Pedestal rocks  ✔
(D) Draas
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Aeolian Abrasion: Genesis of Pedestal Rocks (Mushroom Rocks / Gours): Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Aeolian Abrasion: Genesis of Pedestal Rocks (Mushroom Rocks / Gours) represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): Pedestal rocks.

Yardangs are sculpted into cohesive mudstones or crystalline strata through the synergistic action of aerodynamic sandblasting (abrasion) concentrated within 1–2 meters of the surface, coupled with downwind deflationary evacuation of fine suspended dust.

PART I

Official Examination Question — Question 29
The deltaic structure (topset, foreset, bottomset architecture) is seen on a small-scale in :
(A) Cross-bedding  ✔
(B) Graded bedding
(C) Convolute bedding
(D) Ripple lamination
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Sedimentology & Stratification: Deltaic Clinoform Architecture Reflected in Cross-Bedding: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Sedimentology & Stratification: Deltaic Clinoform Architecture Reflected in Cross-Bedding represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (A): Cross-bedding.

Gilbert-type deltas exhibit a three-fold tripartite architectural hierarchy: horizontal subaerial topset gravels/sands, inclined foreset cross-beds dipping at the angle of repose ($25^\circ-35^\circ$), and flat basinal bottomset clay beds prograding into the receiving basin.

In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (D): old.

William Morris Davis conceptualized landscape evolution as a sequential cycle operating through Youth, Maturity, and Old Age towards a featureless peneplain. 🌐 Q034: Fluvial Hydraulics & Stream Dynamics: Kinetic Energy and Erosive Power Scaling ($E \propto v^2$)

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Arthur Holmes (Principles of Physical Geology, p. 518); Leopold, Wolman & Miller (Fluvial Processes in Geomorphology); Bangar (p. 68)
Official Examination Question — Question 34
The erosive power of a river depends on its velocity. If the velocity is doubled, the erosive power increases by :
(A) two times
(B) four times  ✔
(C) six times
(D) twelve times
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Fluvial Hydraulics & Stream Dynamics: Kinetic Energy and Erosive Power Scaling ($E \propto v^2$): Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Fluvial Hydraulics & Stream Dynamics: Kinetic Energy and Erosive Power Scaling ($E \propto v^2$) represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (B): four times.

A stream's kinetic energy and erosive capability scale quadratically ($E_k \propto v^2$) with mean flow velocity, while its hydraulic competence—the maximum mass of a transportable particle—scales to the sixth power of velocity ($v^6$) according to the Sixth Power Law of Stream Transport.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (B) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Arthur Holmes (Principles of Physical Geology, p. 518); Leopold, Wolman & Miller (Fluvial Processes in Geomorphology); Bangar (p. 68)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$E_k = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 \propto v^2 \quad \text{and} \quad \text{Competence } (M_{\text{max}}) \propto v^6$$

🌐 Q035: Channel Pattern Dynamics: Multichannel Sinuous Anastomosing River Networks

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Smith & Smith (1980); Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology and Stratigraphy, pp. 248–254); Miall (The Geology of Fluvial Deposits)
Official Examination Question — Question 35
An interlaced network of high sinuosity channels separated by stable vegetated islands is a feature exhibited by :
(A) Meandering streams
(B) Braided streams
(C) Anastomosing streams  ✔
(D) Incised meanders
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Channel Pattern Dynamics: Multichannel Sinuous Anastomosing River Networks: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Channel Pattern Dynamics: Multichannel Sinuous Anastomosing River Networks represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): Anastomosing streams.

Centrifugal acceleration and helicoidal cross-channel secondary circulation deflect maximum shear stress ($\tau_{\text{outer}}$) against the outer concave cut bank, inducing continuous lateral migration and point-bar accretion until neck cut-off forms an isolated oxbow lake.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (C) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Smith & Smith (1980); Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology and Stratigraphy, pp. 248–254); Miall (The Geology of Fluvial Deposits)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$v_{\text{outer}} > v_{\text{inner}} \implies \tau_{\text{outer}} > \tau_c \ (\text{Cut Bank Erosion}), \quad \tau_{\text{inner}} < \tau_c \ (\text{Point Bar Deposition})$$

Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics

Centrifugal acceleration and helicoidal cross-channel secondary circulation deflect maximum shear stress ($\tau_{\text{outer}}$) against the outer concave cut bank, inducing continuous lateral migration and point-bar accretion until neck cut-off forms an isolated oxbow lake.

(B) II and IV only

Centrifugal acceleration and helicoidal cross-channel secondary circulation deflect maximum shear stress ($\tau_{\text{outer}}$) against the outer concave cut bank, inducing continuous lateral migration and point-bar accretion until neck cut-off forms an isolated oxbow lake.

🌐 Q049: Glacial Bedrock Landforms: Asymmetrical Abraded Bedrock Mounds (Roches Moutonnées)

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Arthur Holmes (Principles of Physical Geology, pp. 630–635); Thornbury (pp. 365–368); Benn & Evans (Glaciers and Glaciation)
Official Examination Question — Question 49
Low, rounded, streamlined bedrock mounds on glaciated valley floors exhibiting smooth upstream and plucked downstream faces are known as :
(A) Pingos
(B) Roches moutonnées  ✔
(C) Kame Terraces
(D) Drumlins
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Glacial Bedrock Landforms: Asymmetrical Abraded Bedrock Mounds (Roches Moutonnées): Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Glacial Bedrock Landforms: Asymmetrical Abraded Bedrock Mounds (Roches Moutonnées) represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (B): Roches moutonnées.

Roches moutonnées are sculpted by moving subglacial ice across bedrock knolls: the upstream stoss face undergoes high compressive stress and intense striating abrasion, while the downstream lee face experiences localized cavitation and subglacial plucking along unconfined joint blocks.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (B) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Arthur Holmes (Principles of Physical Geology, pp. 630–635); Thornbury (pp. 365–368); Benn & Evans (Glaciers and Glaciation)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\text{Stoss Side: } \sigma_n > 0 \implies \text{Abrasion (Striations/Polish)}; \quad \text{Lee Side: } \sigma_n \rightarrow 0,\ P_w \uparrow \implies \text{Quarrying / Plucking}$$

🌐 Q051: Streamlined Subglacial Till Morphology: Inverted Geometry of Drumlins

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Flint (Glacial and Quaternary Geology); Thornbury (pp. 375–378); Arthur Holmes (p. 642)
Official Examination Question — Question 51
Which of the following subglacial depositional features exhibits a streamlined geometry that is morphologically opposite to roches moutonnées (steep upstream stoss and tapering downstream lee) ?
(A) Drumlins  ✔
(B) Moulins
(C) Pingos
(D) Erratics
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics

Roches moutonnées are sculpted by moving subglacial ice across bedrock knolls: the upstream stoss face undergoes high compressive stress and intense striating abrasion, while the downstream lee face experiences localized cavitation and subglacial plucking along unconfined joint blocks.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (A) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Flint (Glacial and Quaternary Geology); Thornbury (pp. 375–378); Arthur Holmes (p. 642)

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Glen (1955, Glen's Flow Law); Paterson (Physics of Glaciers); Thornbury (pp. 355–358)
Official Examination Question — Question 54
Which of the following statements concerning glacial flow dynamics is NOT correct ?
(A) the surface ice moves faster than basal ice due to frictional retardation at the bed
(B) the middle portion of the glacier moves slower than the margins  ✔
(C) the glacier velocity increases with the thickness and surface slope of the ice
(D) glacial flow velocity increases with ambient ice temperature (temperate vs. cold ice)
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Glacial Ice Dynamics & Flow Mechanics: Velocity Profiles in Valley Glaciers: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Glacial Ice Dynamics & Flow Mechanics: Velocity Profiles in Valley Glaciers represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (B): the middle portion of the glacier moves slower than the margins.

Glacial ice deforms as a non-linear, shear-thinning viscoplastic fluid governed by Glen's Flow Law. Horizontal flow velocity reaches its theoretical maximum at the glacier centerline and upper surface, decreasing with depth towards the bed and margins due to boundary frictional shear.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (B) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Glen (1955, Glen's Flow Law); Paterson (Physics of Glaciers); Thornbury (pp. 355–358)

$$\dot{\epsilon} = A \tau^n \quad [\text{Glen's Flow Law: } n \approx 3], \quad u(z) = u_b + \frac{2A}{n+1} (\rho g \sin\alpha)^n (H^{n+1} - (H-z)^{n+1})$$

🌐 Q088: Glacial Mass Wastage: Mechanics of Total Glacial Ablation

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Paterson (The Physics of Glaciers, Ch. 2); Benn & Evans (Glaciers and Glaciation); Arthur Holmes (p. 620)
Official Examination Question — Question 88
The aggregate process through which glacier mass is lost by the combined actions of melting, evaporation/sublimation, and iceberg calving is :
(A) Nivation
(B) Calvation
(C) Ablation  ✔
(D) Plucking
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Glacial Mass Wastage: Mechanics of Total Glacial Ablation: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Glacial Mass Wastage: Mechanics of Total Glacial Ablation represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): Ablation.

By Archimedes' Principle, a floating body displaces a volume of fluid equal to its total mass. Because glacial freshwater ice has a bulk density of ~0.917 g/cm³ compared to ~1.025 g/cm³ for oceanic seawater, approximately 8/9 of an iceberg's volume remains submerged beneath sea level.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (C) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Paterson (The Physics of Glaciers, Ch. 2); Benn & Evans (Glaciers and Glaciation); Arthur Holmes (p. 620)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\frac{V_{\text{submerged}}}{V_{\text{total}}} = \frac{\rho_{\text{ice}}}{\rho_{\text{seawater}}} = \frac{0.917\text{ g/cm}^3}{1.025\text{ g/cm}^3} \approx 0.895 \implies V_{\text{above}} \approx \frac{1}{9}\ (\sim 10.5\%)$$

🌐 Q091: Deltaic Morphology: Fine-Grained Sedimentation in Digitate / Bird's Foot Deltas

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology and Stratigraphy, pp. 296–304); Thornbury (p. 170); Arthur Holmes (p. 544)
Official Examination Question — Question 91
When river distributaries are few, discharge is confined by muddy levees, and fine-grained silt and clay prograde into a quiet sea, it generates a/an :
(A) Arcuate delta
(B) Cuspate delta
(C) Bird's foot delta  ✔
(D) Elongated delta
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Deltaic Morphology: Fine-Grained Sedimentation in Digitate / Bird's Foot Deltas: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Deltaic Morphology: Fine-Grained Sedimentation in Digitate / Bird's Foot Deltas represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): Bird's foot delta.

Gilbert-type deltas exhibit a three-fold tripartite architectural hierarchy: horizontal subaerial topset gravels/sands, inclined foreset cross-beds dipping at the angle of repose ($25^\circ-35^\circ$), and flat basinal bottomset clay beds prograding into the receiving basin.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (C) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology and Stratigraphy, pp. 296–304); Thornbury (p. 170); Arthur Holmes (p. 544)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\text{Delta Architecture:} \quad \text{Topset (Fluvial-Marsh)} \longrightarrow \text{Foreset (Clinoform Slope)} \longrightarrow \text{Bottomset (Prodelta Basinal Clay)}$$

Official Examination Question — Question 108
Glacial cirques (corries) are initially hollowed out and widened beneath perennial snow patches primarily by the process of :
(A) Nivation  ✔
(B) Calvation
(C) Ablation
(D) Abrasion
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Cirque Initiation & Glacial Morphogenesis: Role of Periglacial Nivation: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Cirque Initiation & Glacial Morphogenesis: Role of Periglacial Nivation represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (A): Nivation.

Roches moutonnées are sculpted by moving subglacial ice across bedrock knolls: the upstream stoss face undergoes high compressive stress and intense striating abrasion, while the downstream lee face experiences localized cavitation and subglacial plucking along unconfined joint blocks.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (A) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Matthes (1900, Glacial Sculpture of the Bighorn Mountains); Thornbury (Principles of Geomorphology, pp. 360–364); Holmes (p. 627)

$$\text{Stoss Side: } \sigma_n > 0 \implies \text{Abrasion (Striations/Polish)}; \quad \text{Lee Side: } \sigma_n \rightarrow 0,\ P_w \uparrow \implies \text{Quarrying / Plucking}$$

(A) Bayou
(B) Chenier  ✔
(C) Panplain
(D) Hamada
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics

Gilbert-type deltas exhibit a three-fold tripartite architectural hierarchy: horizontal subaerial topset gravels/sands, inclined foreset cross-beds dipping at the angle of repose ($25^\circ-35^\circ$), and flat basinal bottomset clay beds prograding into the receiving basin.

Match the following periglacial, fluvioglacial, and hydrological phenomena with their definitions : (A) Bourne ——— (4) A seasonal, intermittent groundwater spring in chalk terranes (B) Talik ———— (3) An unfrozen, permeable ground layer occurring within continuous permafrost (C) Naled ———— (2) A massive sheet of surface icing (aufeis) formed by recurrent freezing of groundwater (D) Os / Esker —— (1) A sinuous, meandering ridge of stratified fluvioglacial sand and gravel
(A) A-4, B-2, C-3, D-1
(B) A-1, B-3, C-2, D-4

Centrifugal acceleration and helicoidal cross-channel secondary circulation deflect maximum shear stress ($\tau_{\text{outer}}$) against the outer concave cut bank, inducing continuous lateral migration and point-bar accretion until neck cut-off forms an isolated oxbow lake.

Official Examination Question — Question 114
When subsurface water from extraneous meteoric or groundwater sources flashes into high-pressure steam upon contact with magma, producing violent explosions without juvenile lava, it is termed a :
(A) Phreatic explosion  ✔
(B) Fissure eruption
(C) Crater eruption
(D) Nuées ardentes
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Hydrovolcanism: Steam-Driven Phreatic (Hydrothermal) Explosions: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Calderas are macroscopic collapse basins formed when rapid catastrophic drainage or violent explosive evacuation of an underlying shallow magma chamber leaves the volcanic edifice roof unsupported, inducing structural ring-fault collapse.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (A) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Cas & Wright (Volcanic Successions, Ch. 5); Macdonald (Volcanoes); Arthur Holmes (p. 254)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\Delta V_{\text{chamber}} \gg \text{Magma Replenishment} \implies \sigma_t > \sigma_{\text{roof}} \implies \text{Piston / Ring-Fracture Collapse}$$

(B) Hamada
(C) Koum

PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Arthur Holmes (pp. 493–498); Blackwelder (1934, Yardangs, GSA Bull.); Thornbury (p. 292)
Official Examination Question — Question 126
Which of the following aeolian physical processes is most fundamental in excavating the parallel windward troughs and keel-shaped ridges of yardangs ?
(A) Attrition
(B) Abrasion  ✔
(C) Deflation
(D) Transportation
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Aeolian Morphodynamics: Wind Sandblasting Abrasion in Yardang Sculpting: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Aeolian Morphodynamics: Wind Sandblasting Abrasion in Yardang Sculpting represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (B): Abrasion.

Yardangs are sculpted into cohesive mudstones or crystalline strata through the synergistic action of aerodynamic sandblasting (abrasion) concentrated within 1–2 meters of the surface, coupled with downwind deflationary evacuation of fine suspended dust.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (B) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Arthur Holmes (pp. 493–498); Blackwelder (1934, Yardangs, GSA Bull.); Thornbury (p. 292)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$q_s \propto (u_* - u_{*t})^3 \quad [\text{Saltation Flux Sandblasting Dominance}]$$

(D) Pediment
PART I

In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): Bajada.

Calderas are macroscopic collapse basins formed when rapid catastrophic drainage or violent explosive evacuation of an underlying shallow magma chamber leaves the volcanic edifice roof unsupported, inducing structural ring-fault collapse.

🌐 Q128: Meander Hydraulics & Sedimentation: Cut Bank Erosion vs. Point Bar Accretion

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Leopold, Wolman & Miller (1964, Fluvial Processes in Geomorphology); Sam Boggs Jr. (pp. 242–248); Holmes (pp. 525–532)
Official Examination Question — Question 128
In a dynamically equilibrium meandering river reach :
(A) The depth and thickness of the channel remains uniform across its entire width
(B) Helicoidal secondary flow causes erosion on the convex inside bend and deposition on the concave outside
(C) Centrifugal force accelerates velocity causing erosion on the concave outer cut-bank and deposition on the convex inner point-bar  ✔
(D) Fine-grained silt settles exclusively on the high-energy cut bank
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Meander Hydraulics & Sedimentation: Cut Bank Erosion vs. Point Bar Accretion: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Meander Hydraulics & Sedimentation: Cut Bank Erosion vs. Point Bar Accretion represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): Centrifugal force accelerates velocity causing erosion on the concave outer cut-bank and deposition on the convex inner point-bar.

Centrifugal acceleration and helicoidal cross-channel secondary circulation deflect maximum shear stress ($\tau_{\text{outer}}$) against the outer concave cut bank, inducing continuous lateral migration and point-bar accretion until neck cut-off forms an isolated oxbow lake.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (C) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Leopold, Wolman & Miller (1964, Fluvial Processes in Geomorphology); Sam Boggs Jr. (pp. 242–248); Holmes (pp. 525–532)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$v_{\text{outer}} > v_{\text{inner}} \implies \tau_{\text{outer}} > \tau_c \ (\text{Cut Bank Erosion}), \quad \tau_{\text{inner}} < \tau_c \ (\text{Point Bar Deposition})$$

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology and Stratigraphy, Ch. 8); Arthur Holmes (p. 535); Thornbury (p. 175)

(A) Alluvial fan  ✔
(B) Stream Terrace
(C) Pediment
(D) Natural levee
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Sedimentary Systems Analogy: Alluvial Fan as the Subaerial Piedmont Counterpart of a Delta: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Sedimentary Systems Analogy: Alluvial Fan as the Subaerial Piedmont Counterpart of a Delta represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (A): Alluvial fan.

Gilbert-type deltas exhibit a three-fold tripartite architectural hierarchy: horizontal subaerial topset gravels/sands, inclined foreset cross-beds dipping at the angle of repose ($25^\circ-35^\circ$), and flat basinal bottomset clay beds prograding into the receiving basin.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (A) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology and Stratigraphy, Ch. 8); Arthur Holmes (p. 535); Thornbury (p. 175)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\text{Delta Architecture:} \quad \text{Topset (Fluvial-Marsh)} \longrightarrow \text{Foreset (Clinoform Slope)} \longrightarrow \text{Bottomset (Prodelta Basinal Clay)}$$

🌐 Q131: Fluvial Hydraulic Mechanics: Cavitation Erosion Induced by Vapor Bubble Collapse

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Barnes (1956, Cavitation in Stream Hydraulics); Leopold, Wolman & Miller (Fluvial Processes in Geomorphology); Bangar (p. 69)
Official Examination Question — Question 131
The sudden, explosive implosion and collapse of vapor bubbles in high-velocity turbulent stream waters, producing extreme localized shock pressures that fracture rock, is :
(A) Solution
(B) Cavitation  ✔
(C) Corrosion
(D) Corrasion
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Fluvial Hydraulic Mechanics: Cavitation Erosion Induced by Vapor Bubble Collapse: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Fluvial Hydraulic Mechanics: Cavitation Erosion Induced by Vapor Bubble Collapse represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (B): Cavitation.

Where turbulent stream velocities exceed ~10–12 m/s over irregular rock steps, localized pressure drops below the saturation vapor pressure of water, nucleating vapor cavities. Immediate advection into higher-pressure zones causes explosive bubble collapse, unleashing microscopic water hammer shockwaves that shatter crystalline bedrock.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (B) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Barnes (1956, Cavitation in Stream Hydraulics); Leopold, Wolman & Miller (Fluvial Processes in Geomorphology); Bangar (p. 69)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$P < P_{\text{vapor}} \implies \text{Bubble Formation}; \quad P > P_{\text{vapor}} \implies \text{Violent Implosion } [P_{\text{shock}} > 1000\text{ MPa}]$$

🌐 Q133: Glacial Drift Classification: Non-Stratified Glacial Till in Drumlins vs. Stratified Glaciofluvial Drift

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Flint (Glacial and Quaternary Geology); Sam Boggs Jr. (pp. 330–338); Thornbury (pp. 374–380)
Official Examination Question — Question 133
Which of the following glacial depositional landforms is composed of unstratified, unsorted glacial till and is therefore NOT a stratified glaciofluvial drift deposit ?
(A) Drumlins  ✔
(B) Eskers
(C) Kames
(D) Varves
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Glacial Drift Classification: Non-Stratified Glacial Till in Drumlins vs. Stratified Glaciofluvial Drift: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Glacial Drift Classification: Non-Stratified Glacial Till in Drumlins vs. Stratified Glaciofluvial Drift represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (A): Drumlins.

Roches moutonnées are sculpted by moving subglacial ice across bedrock knolls: the upstream stoss face undergoes high compressive stress and intense striating abrasion, while the downstream lee face experiences localized cavitation and subglacial plucking along unconfined joint blocks.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (A) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Flint (Glacial and Quaternary Geology); Sam Boggs Jr. (pp. 330–338); Thornbury (pp. 374–380)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\text{Stoss Side: } \sigma_n > 0 \implies \text{Abrasion (Striations/Polish)}; \quad \text{Lee Side: } \sigma_n \rightarrow 0,\ P_w \uparrow \implies \text{Quarrying / Plucking}$$

🌐 Q135: Peneplain Rejuvenation Criteria: Diagnostic Morphological Signatures of Uplifted Peneplains

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Dr. Ausaf Sayeed (Explanatory Note *135, p. 144); W.D. Thornbury (Principles of Geomorphology, pp. 182–190); Arthur Holmes (pp. 480–486)
Official Examination Question — Question 135
Uplifted (rejuvenated) peneplains are definitively diagnosed in geomorphology by one or more of the following criteria : (i) Thick mantle of deeply weathered residual saprolite/soil upon summit surfaces (ii) Regional bevelling and truncation of rock strata of widely varying resistance (iii) Accordant summit levels and superimposed / adapted drainage patterns (iv) Topographic unconformities, incised meanders, and knick points below the summit plateau
(A) (i) and (ii) only
(B) (i) and (iii) only
(C) (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) are all diagnostic  ✔
(D) (ii), (iii) and (iv) only
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Peneplain Rejuvenation Criteria: Diagnostic Morphological Signatures of Uplifted Peneplains: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Peneplain Rejuvenation Criteria: Diagnostic Morphological Signatures of Uplifted Peneplains represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) are all diagnostic.

Centrifugal acceleration and helicoidal cross-channel secondary circulation deflect maximum shear stress ($\tau_{\text{outer}}$) against the outer concave cut bank, inducing continuous lateral migration and point-bar accretion until neck cut-off forms an isolated oxbow lake.

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (C) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Dr. Ausaf Sayeed (Explanatory Note *135, p. 144); W.D. Thornbury (Principles of Geomorphology, pp. 182–190); Arthur Holmes (pp. 480–486)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$v_{\text{outer}} > v_{\text{inner}} \implies \tau_{\text{outer}} > \tau_c \ (\text{Cut Bank Erosion}), \quad \tau_{\text{inner}} < \tau_c \ (\text{Point Bar Deposition})$$

🌐 Q136: Fluvial Pediplanation Theories: Crickmay's Panplain Hypothesis (Lateral Planation)

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Crickmay (1933, The Later Stages of the Cycle of Erosion, Geol. Mag.); Thornbury (pp. 186–188); Bloom (Ch. 12)
Official Examination Question — Question 136
According to C.H. Crickmay (1933), a regional low-relief erosional plain produced by the lateral migration and coalescing floodplains of mature rivers is termed a :
(A) Pediplain
(B) Peneplain
(C) Panplain  ✔
(D) Etch plain
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Fluvial Pediplanation Theories: Crickmay's Panplain Hypothesis (Lateral Planation): Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Fluvial Pediplanation Theories: Crickmay's Panplain Hypothesis (Lateral Planation) represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (C): Panplain.

William Morris Davis conceptualized landscape evolution as a sequential cycle operating through Youth, Maturity, and Old Age towards a featureless peneplain. Walter Penck countered that landforms reflect the simultaneous dynamic interaction between crustal uplift velocity U(t) and denudation rate E(t).

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (C) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Crickmay (1933, The Later Stages of the Cycle of Erosion, Geol. Mag.); Thornbury (pp. 186–188); Bloom (Ch. 12)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\text{Landscape} = f(\text{Structure, Process, Stage}) \quad [\text{Davisian Postulate}] \quad \text{vs.} \quad \frac{dz}{dt} = U(t) - E(t) \quad [\text{Penckian Dynamic Model}]$$

🌐 Q139: Penck's Morphological Analysis: Simultaneous Uplift and Denudation (Endrumpf Concept)

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Walter Penck (1924, Die Morphologische Analyse); Thornbury (Principles of Geomorphology, pp. 190–198); Bloom (Ch. 12)
Official Examination Question — Question 139
In contrast to W.M. Davis, Walter Penck's concept of geomorphic landscape development (Morphological Analysis) asserts that :
(A) Rapid tectonic uplift occurs exclusively before any erosion begins
(B) Denudation cannot operate until crustal uplift has completely terminated
(C) Tectonic uplift and denudation occur simultaneously; landform morphology reflects the ratio of rate of uplift to rate of degradation through phases of waxing, uniform, and waning development  ✔
(D) Dynamic equilibrium is strictly prohibited by thermal crustal contraction
PART I

Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Penck's Morphological Analysis: Simultaneous Uplift and Denudation (Endrumpf Concept): Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Calderas are macroscopic collapse basins formed when rapid catastrophic drainage or violent explosive evacuation of an underlying shallow magma chamber leaves the volcanic edifice roof unsupported, inducing structural ring-fault collapse.

(A) Topographic anomaly
(B) Bouguer anomaly
(C) Inversion of topography  ✔
(D) Basin and range topography
PART I

Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics

William Morris Davis conceptualized landscape evolution as a sequential cycle operating through Youth, Maturity, and Old Age towards a featureless peneplain. Walter Penck countered that landforms reflect the simultaneous dynamic interaction between crustal uplift velocity U(t) and denudation rate E(t).

🌐 Q145: Extensional Tectonics & Block Faulting: Genesis of Basin and Range Topography

Source: Objective Geology for Civil Services & Competitive Exams Authoritative Reference: Dr. Ausaf Sayeed (Explanatory Note *145, p. 144); Gilbert (1928, Basin Range Faulting, USGS Prof. Pap. 153); Thornbury (pp. 252–258)
Official Examination Question — Question 145
The world-famous 'Basin and Range' topography of the North American Cordillera is dynamically produced by :
(A) Faulting (regional crustal extension producing tilted fault-block ranges and graben valleys)  ✔
(B) Folding
(C) Jointing
(D) All of the above
PART I
Theoretical Foundation & Scientific Principles
Authoritative textbook grounding, analytical derivations, and physical mechanics
Extensional Tectonics & Block Faulting: Genesis of Basin and Range Topography: Fundamental Principles & Mechanics

Extensional Tectonics & Block Faulting: Genesis of Basin and Range Topography represents a foundational concept in physical geology, process geomorphology, and sedimentary dynamics. In Dr. Ausaf Sayeed's Objective Geology, the officially verified answer is firmly established as Option (A): Faulting (regional crustal extension producing tilted fault-block ranges and graben valleys).

William Morris Davis conceptualized landscape evolution as a sequential cycle operating through Youth, Maturity, and Old Age towards a featureless peneplain. Walter Penck countered that landforms reflect the simultaneous dynamic interaction between crustal uplift velocity U(t) and denudation rate E(t).

"In physical geology and process geomorphology: Option (A) represents the universally verified physical standard." — Dr. Ausaf Sayeed (Explanatory Note *145, p. 144); Gilbert (1928, Basin Range Faulting, USGS Prof. Pap. 153); Thornbury (pp. 252–258)
Governing Physical / Mathematical Relationship
$$\text{Landscape} = f(\text{Structure, Process, Stage}) \quad [\text{Davisian Postulate}] \quad \text{vs.} \quad \frac{dz}{dt} = U(t) - E(t) \quad [\text{Penckian Dynamic Model}]$$
